metadata.title: Planar Keller Maps after the Counterexample: Weight-Class Exclusions, a Chart Atlas for the (72,108) Reduction, and Independent Checks of Cases 1 and 2
metadata.description:
The July 2026 counterexample settled the Jacobian conjecture in every dimension N ≥ 3 and left the planar case JC(2) open. This paper studies the planar case in exact arithmetic. Four exclusion theorems follow from a weight-class calculus: a two-term P = x + a x^u y^v is never a Keller component, nor is any lower-weight perturbation of it; no component has a Newton top edge anchored at the linear vertex x with interior direction; and if x is a vertex of the Newton polygon then P = x + f(y). A fifth exclusion, the transport of the Keller constant along the staircase that swallows x, is proved at every partner degree for six certified grid shapes. For the single degree pair (72,108) left open below 125, the reduction of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui has two coefficient systems, Cases 1 and 2. We give a chart atlas of determinantal strata that closes four-coefficient sub-families of Case 1 exactly, an independent derivation of Helali's equations in which Case 2 is proved empty and Case 1 reduces to the unit ideal at five primes, and the measured cost of a Case 1 certificate: exact standard bases did not finish in six hours, and multi-modular certificates exceed 20,000 primes. Case 1 is not closed, so (72,108) and JC(2) remain open. Every result is marked machine-verified, derived or conjectural.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/algebraic-geometry/jacobian-conjecture).
metadata.version_notes: Full revision. Methods: six algorithms with parameters, costs, software and checksums. Proofs: complete proofs of the four exclusion theorems and of the tower lemma. Scope: the all-degree fifth exclusion is stated on its six certified grid shapes and the tower lemma excludes pure-power tops. The (72,108) part is restructured around Proposition 4.3 of Guccione, Guccione, Horruitiner and Valqui: the three branches are mapped onto Cases 1 and 2, the chart atlas is a table of one row per record, and the independent checks of Helali's claim are followed by the measured cost of an exact Case 1 certificate (exact standard bases did not finish in six hours; multi-modular certificates exceed 20,000 primes per branch). The truncation ladder is restated: no covector of degree 1, 2 or 3, minimal degree at least 4, no finite ceiling, the sl2 premise refuted. New: frontier ladder table, exclusion-scope table, related work with 31 references, six figures. The incidence-map description of the counterexample is credited to T. Tao's public digestion (2026-07-21); the programme re-verified it in EXP-086 to EXP-090 and its extension across n is the programme's own. Correction: the half-plane tower, stated as proved in v0.36, is restated as certificates at the sampled windows with propagation to all partner degrees conjectured; the tail steps of the exclusion theorems are derived top-down; the degree-one covector exclusion is modulo one prime (2147483629). The title names the Case 1 and Case 2 results.
